questions.question: Summarise the Term 4 work on circuits, settlement energy and illegal connections, cells and solar cells, and electricity generation and the grid.
questions.expected_answer: Circuits need an input device such as a cell, generator or solar panel, an output such as a lamp, buzzer, motor, heater or resistor, and a control switch, drawn with standard symbols including the cell's long thin positive and short thick negative lines, the lamp's crossed circle, the resistor's rectangle, the open switch, the buzzer's half-circle and the LED with its series resistor, with straight lines, right angles and dots at true junctions; series components share voltage and fail together, parallel components each have full voltage and survive a failure, a short circuit is a near-zero-resistance bypass that heats dangerously, and polarity matters for cells, LEDs and buzzers. Settlement households need heating, lighting, cooking and phone charging from wood, paraffin, candles, gas, solar or the grid, judged on cost, safety, health, convenience and environment, stacking fuels because the cheap options are dangerous, so solutions must change the economics; illegal connections arise from absence, cost and waiting and lack the meter, earth, breaker and earth-leakage protection that stop faults, causing shock, fire and burnt transformers, with an ethical balance of need, law, fairness, safety and responsibility resolved by removing dangerous wires and delivering legal supply, written up as a balanced report with a question title, sourced background, all views, criteria-based discussion, reasoned conclusion and neutral attribution. Cells have two electrodes and an electrolyte with chemistry fixing voltage and size fixing capacity, primary cells dying and secondary recharging, series adding voltage and parallel adding capacity with matched cells; solar cells free electrons across a silicon junction at half a volt each, so panels connect cells in series, output falls with shade, dust, heat and poor angle, systems add a charge controller, battery and inverter, and free clean durable fuel is weighed against night, winter, storage and up-front cost. Thermal stations boil water to steam to spin a turbine and generator at about forty percent efficiency, with coal local, cheap and dirtiest, gas cleaner, flexible and imported, nuclear clean in operation but costly with waste and risk, and solar thermal storing heat in salt; hydro uses head times flow but South Africa lacks rivers, pumped storage stores cheap night power for the evening peak, and wind is cheap and variable and pairs with storage; the grid uses AC at 50 hertz so transformers can step voltage up to 400 kilovolts to cut losses and down to 132, 11 and 230 volts, with frequency at 50 hertz the balance that load shedding protects.

questions.question: Summarise the Term 4 work on Ohm's law and resistors, logic gates and truth tables, and the panic button design project.
questions.expected_answer: Voltage in volts is the push, current in amps the flow and resistance in ohms the squeeze; with resistance unchanged more cells in series raise voltage and current and brighten the lamp, and with voltage unchanged more resistance lowers current and dims it, shown by a fair test that changes one variable, measures current, controls the lamp and wires and honestly records the filament's rising resistance; the ammeter goes in series and never across a cell, the voltmeter across a component; the colour code reads digit, digit, zeros so brown black brown is 100 ohms and orange orange brown 330; series resistances add and current falls, parallel totals drop below the smallest branch and current rises with full voltage per branch, drawn respectively as rectangles in a line without dots and stacked between rails with junction dots. Logic signals are 0 or 1 and a gate has inputs, an output and a rule; AND is series switches with output 1 only when all inputs are 1, a D-shaped symbol, used for interlocks; OR is parallel switches with output 1 when any input is 1, a shield-shaped symbol, used for alarms; a truth table has a column per input and one for output with binary-ordered rows for every combination, four for two inputs and eight for three, AND showing a single 1 at the bottom and OR a single 0 at the top, differing only in mixed rows, every row tested predicted against observed. The panic button project investigates the need with who, where, when and what and the user's voice, writes a brief as problem, users and purpose naming the need not the circuit, lists testable specifications such as any one of three buttons, large and low, loud and bright, battery powered, dark-findable, a reset and a year's standby alongside constraints of kit, budget, low voltage, time and weatherproofing, reads the specification as a three-input OR of three parallel push switches with buzzer and lamp in parallel, an LED with 330 ohm resistor, a reset toggle and zero standby drawn with standard symbols and six dots, writes the eight-row table with one 0 and seven 1s, builds and tests every row plus loudness, reset and standby, and designs an honest bilingual poster with one message, one action, headline, picture, benefits and contact evaluated by the ten-second test.

questions.question: Summarise the Term 3 work on gears, mechanical advantage and the headgear project, and set out the examination craft for the end-of-year paper.
questions.expected_answer: Gears are toothed wheels transferring rotation; meshing gears turn in opposite directions, a small driver turning a large driven gear gives slower output with more turning force and the reverse gives speed, an idler restores direction without changing ratio, and bevel gears turn the axis through ninety degrees; mechanical advantage is output force over input force, for gears driven teeth over driver teeth and for levers the ratio of distances from the pivot, with values above one multiplying force at the cost of distance or speed; gear systems are drawn with templates and described by input-process-output systems diagrams; the mine headgear is a triangulated frame holding the sheave wheel over the shaft for the winder's rope and cage, and the tender project ran from scenario and brief through sketches, working drawing, budget, scale model and presentation, with mining impact, indigenous iron-working and gender bias considered. For the examination, practise drawing symbols and gear diagrams with a ruler until automatic; know the terms input, output, control, series, parallel, step-up, step-down, mechanical advantage and truth table; answer explain questions in full sentences with a reason for each mark; give both advantages and disadvantages in equal number; show formula, substitution and answer in calculations; follow the practised structures for briefs and truth tables; read each question twice and underline the command word; allocate time by marks; answer everything; check diagrams for dots, polarity and labels and tables for the right number of rows; and reread long answers in the final minutes for a reason in every sentence.
